• They need a **medium to propagate** and will not travel through a vacuum.
 
• Sound travels at different speeds in different media.
 
• The speed of sound is determined by the **density (ρ)** and** compressibility (K) **of the medium.
 
• Density is the amount of material in a given volume, and compressibility is a measure of how much a substance could be compacted for a given pressure.
 
• The speed of sound can also be **affected by temperature**. 
 
• Sound waves tend to travel faster at higher temperatures.

• **Water is much denser than air.**
 
• The speed of sound in a medium can be determined by the equation.

 
• v = (Kρ)-½
 
• where v is the speed of sound,
 
• K is the compressibility, and
 
• ρ (rho) is the density.

questions.question: In the field of computing, what does ENIAC stand for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ENIAC stands for **Electronic Numerical Integrator And Computer.**
 
• It is considered to be the first operational electronic digital computer in the United States, developed by **Army Ordnance to compute World War II ballistic firing tables. **
 
• The first all-electric computing machine was proposed by physicist John Mauchly in **1942** and was completed in** 1945**.
 
• The ENIAC weighed **30 tons, used 200 kilowatts of electric power and consisted of 18,000 vacuum tubes, 1,500 relays, and hundreds of thousands of resistors**, capacitors, and inductors.
 
• The ENIAC used** 20 single-number accumulators **as primary functional units.
 
• The ENIAC's field of the application included weather prediction, atomic-energy calculations, cosmic-ray studies, thermal ignition, random-number studies, wind-tunnel design, and other scientific uses.

questions.question: Most of the atmospheric Ozone gas is found in which layer of the atmosphere?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Stratosphere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Ninety percent of the ozone gas in the atmosphere is occupied by the stratosphere, the layer of the atmosphere between about 10 and 50 kilometers altitude. **
 
• The natural level of ozone gas in the stratosphere is a result of a balance between sunlight that **creates ozone gas and chemical reactions that destroy it.**
 
• The Earth's atmosphere consists of several layers.
 
 
• The lowest layer, the troposphere, extends from the Earth's surface up to about **10 kilometers **in altitude. 
 
• The next layer, the stratosphere, continues from 10 km to about 50 km. 
 
• **Ozone is a molecule that contains three oxygen atoms**.
 
 
• ** Ozone molecules are constantly formed and destroyed in the stratosphere**. 
 
• The ozone layer in the stratosphere absorbs a portion of the radiation from the sun, preventing it from reaching the planet's surface. 
 
• It absorbs the portion of the UV light called UVB.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Thermosphere:-**

 
• **The thermosphere is the layer in the Earth's atmosphere directly above the mesosphere and below the exosphere. **
 
• Within this layer of the atmosphere, ultraviolet radiation causes photoionization/photodissociation of molecules, creating ions, the thermosphere thus constitutes the larger part of the ionosphere.

**Mesosphere:-**

 
• **The mesosphere is directly above the stratosphere and below the thermosphere**.
 
• It extends from about 31 to 53 miles above our planet.
 
• Temperature decreases with height throughout the mesosphere.

**Troposphere:-**

 
• **The troposphere is the lowest layer of Earth's atmosphere and the site of all weather on Earth**.
 
• The troposphere is bounded on the top by a layer of air called the tropopause, which separates the troposphere from the stratosphere, and on the bottom by the surface of the Earth.
